name: code_reindex
description: Rebuild the code index of the calling session's own repo (runs gitnexus analyze detached; its output is captured to <data>/code-index/<slug>/analyze.log). Returns after the first tick -- outcome "started" (lock held, process alive, output seen), "up-to-date", "starting" (running, no tick yet), "already-running", or "not-started" with a typed reason (npx-not-found, gitnexus-not-found, analyze-failed, spawn-failed, remote-member, gitnexus-too-old, provider-not-supported); every result also carries injectedBlockFiles (agent docs still holding a gitnexus block from an earlier plain analyze run; never edited). Only the gitnexus provider is supported: provider none fails with E-CODE-INTEL-DISABLED, any other provider (e.g. codebase-memory, which manages its own index) gets not-started with reason provider-not-supported naming the provider. Poll code_status for completion. Scope: always the calling session's own repo -- a member session uses its registered work folder; any other session uses the first MCP client root (roots/list) inside a git repository with an origin remote, as that repository's top level -- the same repository its kb_* tools use -- or the fleet server's working folder when the client offers no roots. Extension for code tools only: when roots are offered and none has an origin remote, the first offered git repository is used (kb_* tools then fail with E-SELF-NO-REMOTE). There is no repo/path scope argument. Fails with E-SELF-NO-WORKFOLDER or E-SELF-NOT-A-REPO when that folder is missing or is not a git repository, E-CODE-INDEX-NOT-READY when it has no usable code index yet (a missing or interrupted index gets a build requested automatically -- retry shortly) or the index is still building (that error's text and structuredContent carry retry_after_ms -- wait that long once, retry once, then fall back; never poll code_status in a loop -- plus retry_will_help and, while an analyze runs, its progress), and E-CODE-INTEL-DISABLED when code intelligence is off (each with a one-line remediation).
